drug: Anktiva (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln) + BCG - papillary-only NMIBC
indication: With BCG, adults with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC); the indication now includes high-grade papillary-only tumors as well as carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors
headline: The FDA approved an expanded indication for Anktiva (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln) with BCG on October 14, 2026, adding adults with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer with high-grade papillary-only tumors to the existing CIS indication. The goal date was January 6, 2027, so the action came 84 days early. ImmunityBio announced the approval the same day.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval notification is dated October 14, 2026 and states the approval was made that day; it revises the 2024 indication (BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS, with or without papillary tumors) to include patients with high-grade papillary-only tumors (FDA approval notification). The goal date was January 6, 2027: ImmunityBio's 8-K exhibit of August 4, 2026 says the FDA accepted the sBLA "for ANKTIVA plus BCG in patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with papillary disease without CIS" and assigned that PDUFA date (ImmunityBio 8-K exhibit, August 4, 2026). Both dates come from documents that state them, so the action came 84 days before the goal date. Per the FDA, efficacy was previously shown in Cohort A of QUILT-3.032 (NCT03022825), 77 patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS: complete response rate 62% (95% CI 51 to 73), with 58% of responders lasting 12 months or more. The FDA extended that result to papillary-only disease on review of the available scientific information, citing the overlapping clinical features of the two tumor types, rather than on a new trial. The FDA also issued a press announcement the same day, calling Anktiva the first FDA-approved treatment specifically for patients with BCG-unresponsive, high-grade papillary-only disease (FDA press announcement, October 14, 2026). ImmunityBio announced the approval on October 14, 2026 (8-K exhibit 99.1). The FDA says full prescribing information will be posted on Drugs@FDA; the letter had not been posted there when this page was published.
source_label: FDA approval notification, nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC, October 14, 2026
h1: Anktiva (nogapendekin alfa) FDA approval for papillary-only NMIBC: Oct 14, 2026
